*Last Updated on August 28, 2026 by Tsenta*


[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) is the top tool to apply to hundreds of jobs automatically and track where you stand in 2026, submitting tailored applications across 19 ATSes.


If you are trying to apply to hundreds of[jobs automatically](https://tsenta.com/jobs) and still know where you stand with every application, the category splits fast. Some tools mainly track. Some tools mainly autofill. A smaller group actually submits applications for you. Tsenta ranks first because it handles the full workflow: find, prep, apply, and track. It surfaces roles from company career pages, tailors your résumé per role, submits across supported employer systems, and gives you a receipt and tracker so you are not guessing what went out.


## What Is a Tool That Auto-Applies to Jobs and Tracks Your Status?


A tool in this category helps you submit large numbers of job applications while keeping a live record of what happened after each send. The difference between products is huge. Some only speed up form filling. Some only track jobs after you manually applied. The strongest products do both: they find relevant openings, tailor materials, submit applications, and then track statuses and replies in one place. Tsenta is built for that full workflow, which is why it fits this search intent better than tracker-only or autofill-only alternatives.


## Why Use Tools to Apply to Hundreds of Jobs and Track Your Status?


Manual applying breaks down when you are running a high-volume search. Research using a large Dice.com application dataset found that 41% of applications arrive within the first[48 hours](https://www.nber.org/papers/w32320) , which is a reason to monitor new postings closely. For new grads, international students on OPT, and early-career tech candidates, the problem is not just finding enough roles. It is getting tailored applications out quickly enough and keeping the tracker clean after dozens or hundreds of submissions.


### What Problems Do These Tools Solve?


- Slow manual submissions across repetitive ATS forms
- Missed roles because the posting went live while you were offline
- Generic applications that trade speed for relevance
- Messy spreadsheets that stop reflecting your real status


The best tools solve all four. Tsenta is strongest here because it is an agent, not a shortcut that only carries your name and email into a form. It monitors company career pages, rewrites your résumé against the job description, submits the application on supported employer systems, and stores the successful submission in your tracker. You choose review-oriented or more automated behavior. You stop doing the repetitive part by hand.


## What to Look for in a Tool That Auto-Applies and Tracks Job Status


The search intent here is specific. You do not want a browser extension that only fills basic fields. You want software that can submit large volumes, work on real applicant tracking system portals, tailor documents, and show you exactly where each application stands afterward. That means evaluating coverage, tracking quality, tailoring depth, and pricing honesty instead of just looking at the biggest application number on a landing page.


### Which Features Actually Matter?


- Real ATS submission, not just job-board autofill
- Broad ATS coverage, especially Workday, Greenhouse, and Lever
- Per-role tailored résumé support
- Application receipts and a usable tracker
- Transparent pricing and realistic application caps


This is where Tsenta separates itself. It covers 19 ATSes, including systems widely used for company-hosted applications. It also publishes straightforward pricing, starts with 25 free applications and no card, and keeps the submitted record visible after the fact. Several alternatives do one or two of these jobs well. Fewer do all of them in one place.


## How Job Seekers Use These Tools to Apply at Scale in 2026


Most serious users combine volume with selectivity. They set role, location, and compensation filters, let a tool surface or submit high-fit jobs, then review the tracker for patterns. Which titles reply? Which companies stall at application review? Which résumé variant converts better? The tool is not the strategy by itself. The tool makes the strategy operational at scale.


Tsenta fits that workflow especially well because the same agent handles discovery, tailoring, submission, and tracking. That matters when you are running a search across dozens of companies at once. It is much easier to learn from outcomes when your match feed, receipts, and tracker live in one system instead of being split across three different apps. If you want a deeper product walkthrough, the public pages on how Tsenta works and pricing are the right next step.

### 2. JobCopilot


JobCopilot is one of the more credible cloud appliers in the category. Its pricing page highlights automated job applications, a job application tracker, AI résumé tailoring, and up to 50 daily job matches on higher tiers. It is a solid option for users who want an ongoing automated search flow and a built-in tracker in the same account.


**Key Features**


- Automated job applications
- Job application tracker
- AI résumé builder and cover letter builder
- Multiple copilots and daily job matches on higher tiers


**Job Search Offerings**


- Automated applications
- Saved applications for review
- Hiring-manager contact credits on higher plans


**Pricing**


- Elite plan starts from $1.05 per day
- Weekly, monthly, and quarterly billing available


**Pros**


- Includes tracking and application automation in one platform
- Broader feature set than a pure tracker
- Flexible billing cadence


**Cons**


- Public pricing is framed around daily rates and plan configuration, which is less straightforward than Tsenta
- Match-based volume may feel narrower for users who want broad ATS-first coverage across company career pages


### 3. AIApply


AIApply is a broader AI job search suite that combines résumé generation, cover letters, interview prep, a job board, and Auto-Apply. It can submit applications for you, and it keeps a record of every application in the product. That makes it relevant for this query, especially if you want more writing and prep tooling around the application engine.


**Key Features**


- Auto-Apply for outbound applications
- AI résumé builder and cover letter generator
- ATS résumé scanner
- Interview prep tools
- Job board and application records


**Job Search Offerings**


- Tailored application documents
- Credit-based application submissions
- In-product history of sent applications


**Pricing**


- Core premium subscription sold separately from Auto-Apply credits
- Auto-Apply credits offered in packs such as 100 or 250


**Pros**


- Wide feature surface beyond applying alone
- Good fit for users who want documents, prep, and application sending in one suite
- Flexible pay-for-volume model for auto-apply usage


**Cons**


- Pricing is more modular and can be harder to forecast than Tsenta
- Product emphasis is broader than pure ATS submission and status tracking


### 4. LoopCV


LoopCV remains a common choice for job seekers who want automated outreach at a lower starting price. The platform says it scans 30+ job boards daily, matches jobs to your CV, submits applications automatically, and includes an application dashboard. It also notes that some external-site applications may still require manual handling, which is an important limitation to understand.


**Key Features**


- Automated job applications
- Application dashboard
- CV matching
- Browser extension for login-based flows
- Follow-up email support


**Job Search Offerings**


- Free plan with automated applications
- Paid plans with higher application volume and priority processing


**Pricing**


- Free plan available
- Paid plans start at €9.99/month


**Pros**


- Lower-cost entry point than many competitors
- Includes tracking dashboard and automation together
- Free plan lowers the barrier to trying the category


**Cons**


- Coverage depends heavily on supported job boards and paths
- Some external redirects still require manual application work


### 5. Sonara


Sonara positions itself as an AI-powered job search automation platform that continuously finds and applies to relevant openings. Its messaging is simple and high-volume, which appeals to users who want a more hands-off setup. It belongs on this list because it is a real auto-apply product, even if its public pages are lighter on the kind of transparent workflow detail some users want before trusting an agent with large-scale submissions.


**Key Features**


- Continuous job search automation
- AI-powered matching
- Automated applications


**Job Search Offerings**


- Find jobs for you
- Apply on your behalf
- Ongoing matched-role workflow


**Pricing**


- Pricing details are not clearly surfaced on the main public page


**Pros**


- Clear focus on hands-off automation
- Simple user-facing positioning


**Cons**


- Less public clarity on pricing and tracking specifics
- Harder to evaluate submission transparency before signup


### 6. Simplify


Simplify is one of the best tracker-plus-autofill tools, and it is worth including because many people searching for auto-apply tools start here. Simplify Copilot can autofill applications on over 100 job boards and portals, and the company says its autofill, application tracker, job matches, and basic résumé builder are free. That is strong value. The trade-off is category fit: Simplify helps with filling and tracking, but it is not the same thing as a true end-to-end submission agent.


**Key Features**


- Autofill across 100+ job boards and portals
- Application tracker
- Job matches
- Basic résumé builder


**Job Search Offerings**


- Browser-based application assistance
- Free tracking workflow
- AI-generated responses in supported settings


**Pricing**


- Core autofill, tracker, matches, and basic résumé builder are free


**Pros**


- Excellent free value
- Strong tracker for users still applying manually
- Broad browser-extension footprint


**Cons**


- Primarily a form-fill and workflow tool, not a full application agent
- You still handle meaningful parts of many submissions yourself


### 7. Teal


Teal is a strong choice if your real goal is organization rather than automated submission. Its job tracker is mature, its résumé tools are popular, and it offers unlimited job tracking on free membership. For users who want to track every application, contact, and next step while tailoring documents manually, Teal remains one of the cleaner products in the space.


**Key Features**


- Job application tracker
- Résumé builder
- Keyword matching and analysis
- Chrome extension for saving jobs


**Job Search Offerings**


- Unlimited job tracking
- Multiple résumé versions
- AI-assisted résumé content on paid plans


**Pricing**


- Free plan available
- Teal+ starts at $13 per week, with monthly and quarterly options


**Pros**


- Very good tracker and résumé workflow
- Free plan is genuinely useful
- Good visibility into search progress


**Cons**


- Does not solve the actual submission workload end to end
- Better for managing a search than applying at high volume automatically


### 8. Huntr


Huntr is another tracker-first tool that deserves a place because it is one of the more fully developed job search CRMs for individuals. It offers job tracking, contact management, document storage, AI tailoring features, and application autofills. If you care most about pipeline hygiene and keeping every job, note, and contact in one place, Huntr is a serious option. It ranks lower for this query because it is stronger on tracking than on true large-scale automated applying.


**Key Features**


- Job tracker
- Contact and document management
- Chrome job clipper
- AI tailored résumés and cover letters on Pro
- Application autofills


**Job Search Offerings**


- Track up to 100 jobs on free plan
- Unlimited job tracking on Pro
- CRM-style workflow for applications and contacts


**Pricing**


- Basic: $0/month
- Pro: $40/month
- Quarterly and biannual billing available


**Pros**


- One of the best products for structured tracking
- Good document and contact organization
- Useful if your search includes lots of networking and follow-up


**Cons**


- Less aligned with users who want a tool to actually submit hundreds of applications for them
- Higher monthly price than Tsenta while solving a different, narrower problem

## FAQs About Tools to Auto-Apply to Hundreds of Jobs and Track Your Status


### Why do job seekers need tools that auto-apply and track job applications?


High-volume job searching creates two problems at once: submitting enough tailored applications fast enough, and remembering what happened after each send. Tsenta addresses both. It can surface roles from company career pages, submit across supported employer systems, and keep receipts and tracker records for successful applications. That matters most for users applying across dozens or hundreds of roles, where manual follow-up and spreadsheet tracking usually fall apart well before the search is over.


### What is the difference between an autofill tool and an application agent?


An autofill tool helps carry your saved data into forms faster. You still find the role, open the application, sign in, move through screens, review questions, and submit manually. An application agent goes further and completes the submission workflow on your behalf. Tsenta is an agent. That distinction matters because users searching for the best AI tools that automatically apply to jobs and track every application usually want the second category, not just faster typing.


### What are the best tools to apply to hundreds of jobs automatically and track every application?


The strongest options in 2026 are Tsenta, JobCopilot, AIApply, LoopCV, Sonara, Simplify, Teal, and Huntr. The right choice depends on what you actually need. If you want true end-to-end submission plus tracking, Tsenta is the most complete fit. If you mainly want a tracker, Teal and Huntr are strong. If you want lower-cost automation on job boards, LoopCV can be worth considering. The category split matters more than the headline claim.


### Can these tools guarantee interviews or job offers?


No. Any honest tool should be clear about that. These products can improve speed, increase volume, reduce repetitive work, and keep your search organized. They cannot control recruiter decisions. Tsenta is useful because it controls what software actually can control: job discovery timing, tailored materials, submission speed, and tracking visibility. Recruiters still decide who moves forward. That is the right expectation to keep when choosing any auto-apply or job-tracking platform.
